text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Thursday.

GERMANY - German Bunds fell to heavy losses as fresh economic data added to concern that U.S. economic activity was gaining pace. The March Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 99.50 down, 1.29 from Tuesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - UK gilts slumped into the close, spooked by another sharp fall in U.S. Treasuries after stronger-than- expected NAPM survey, traders said attention totally focused on U.S. and growing chances of February rate rise. The March long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 108-17/32, down 1.13/32 from Tuesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - A weak U.S. bond market continued to dominate French bonds, sending the March bond future down to its lowest closing level since November 25. The March notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 127.92, down 0.40 from Tuesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bonds and Btp futures slumped with other debt markets on the first trading day of the New Year, sliding through several support levels in a thin market as U.S. T-bonds fell after U.S. December NAPM data triggered a sell-off. The March bond future on LIFFE was trading at 127.50, down 1.90 from Tuesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries stay depressed with T-bonds down more than 1 percent, rise in December NAPM to 54.0 from 52.7 in November triggers the selloff, March bond contract falls through December low, with no new buyers seen given two days in a row of strong data, sharp declines in stock prices add to bond market woes. The March Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 111-18/32, down 1.02/32 from Tuesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.73 percent.
JAPAN - The Japanese bond market was closed for a National Holiday. In after hours trading the March future on LIFFE was trading at 123.80.

EUROBONDS - A number of mark Eurobonds were launched, to the surprise of some bankers who said weak government bond markets could hurt the deals. Falls in the U.S. Treasury market on December 31 caused by signs of a pick-up in economic activity triggered a sharp decline in German Bunds on Thursday. The new issue most likely to be affected was DSL Finance's 1.0 billion mark 10-year benchmark bond, which was priced to yield 25 b.p. over Bunds, dealers said.
